title: check critic is two paths under one name -- a corpus sweep here, a staged zero at Baize, same vendored bytes
body:
# 0018: check critic is two paths under one name -- a corpus sweep here, a staged zero at Baize, same vendored bytes

## Tags

check, critic, staged, corpus, dispatch, seals

## Summary

On 2026-08-24, after the fleet sweep made every install's vendored bytes identical (source_commit 591f73ed), the same command examined different things in different trees. In devbin's own checkout, `bin/devbin check critic` with nothing staged sealed green over a CORPUS sweep -- "ok: no shell findings at severity >= warning across 27 file(s)", with a rules-ASKED preamble and NO nothing-staged warning anywhere, terminal or seal. At Baize, `bin/baize check critic` with nothing staged sealed green over ZERO files -- "ok: no staged <lang> files to scan" once per declared language, with the warning at line 1 of the sealed .out. Both runs are honest about what they did. They did different things under one name.

## Reproduction

Both directions measured 2026-08-24, nothing staged in either tree (verified by `git diff --cached --name-only` before each run). Devbin: seal pair tmp/check/20260824-1052.critic.{out,errors}, 0 bytes errors, 27 files examined. Baize: tmp/check/20260824-1055.CRITIC.{out,errors}, 0 bytes errors, zero files, warning present (measured by baize-vc). Note the case difference in the seal names -- `.critic.` here, `.CRITIC.` there -- which may itself be a clue about which code path minted each.

## Root Cause

Unread, deliberately -- this issue records the measurement, not a theory. The builtin `builtin_check_critic` defaults to `--staged` and warns on an empty staged set (lib/cmd/check:132-137); something in the dispatch or configuration difference between the D12 checkout and an installed project either bypasses that branch or routes to a different invocation entirely. The cc board's 2026-08-10 note describes zero-file staged behavior in this tree; the 08-19..08-21 check-critic commits (bd2bc4d, 89b02c5, ca53b76) reshaped this area. Read the dispatch (resolve, gatecmd, the catalogue row `check.critic any critic CRITIC - @builtin`) in BOTH tree shapes before proposing anything.

## Mechanism -- READ 2026-08-24 (vc), and it refutes this issue's own hypothesis

Not the dispatch, and not the tree shape. **`bin/.devbin/cmd/check` is a PROJECT handler that exists in exactly one tree in the fleet, and that tree is devbin's own.**

    for p in ~/Devel/prj/*/bin/.devbin/cmd/check; do [ -e "$p" ] && echo "$p"; done
    -> Devbin/bin/.devbin/cmd/check          (and nothing else)

A project handler displaces the whole built-in option set, which is D5 working exactly as designed and is covered by an existing test of that name. So:

| Tree            | `check critic` resolves to                | Corpus                          | Seal        |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------- |
| **devbin**      | `bin/.devbin/cmd/check`, `gate_critic`    | `intent critic shell --files ...` | `.critic.`  |
| every other install | catalogue `@builtin`, `builtin_check_critic` | defaults to `--staged`        | `.CRITIC.`  |

The handler calls `run_gate --label "rules (intent critic shell)" --suffix critic`, and that **lowercase `--suffix critic` is the case clue this issue flagged** -- devbin's config declares `log: CRITIC`, so an uppercase seal could only have come from the catalogue path. The seal name was reading out which implementation ran, before anyone knew there were two.

`gate_critic` passes an explicit `--files` corpus and therefore never reaches the `--staged` default or its nothing-staged warning. Both behaviours are correct for the code that produced them; neither is reachable from the other.

**The handler is dated 2026-08-06 and `lib/cmd/check` 2026-08-21.** It is not a divergence from the builtin -- it PREDATES it by two weeks, and was simply never retired when the framework grew its own.

**A second finding, from the same reading:** devbin's `bin/.devbin/config.yaml` declares `check.{syntax,lint,critic}` with `run: devbin-internal-syntax`, `devbin-internal-lint` and `devbin-internal-critic`. Those three names resolve to nothing anywhere in the repository, and they never execute, because the project handler displaces them. They are dead `run:` targets sitting in **the config the documentation points at as the worked example**.

## Impact

A reader cannot know from the command name which contract ran: "check critic passed" means examined-everything in one tree and examined-what-was-staged in another. Neither is a false green -- both seals state their scope in the .out -- but the scope statement is the only difference between a comprehensive verdict and a vacuous one, which is exactly the weight a one-line scope statement should not have to carry alone (see 0019).

## Proposed Fix

Establish the mechanism by reading, then either make one name mean one contract, or make the contract an explicit, documented axis (eg staged-by-default everywhere, corpus under a flag) so the divergence is a choice with a name rather than an accident of tree shape.

## Related

- 0019 -- the reading-order half: where the scope fact lives vs where the verdict lives
- 0016 -- the 08-17 rework of this function's failure diagnoses
- cc/wip.md watch-out "BEFORE RAISING A DEFECT, CHECK WHETHER THE CODE ALREADY RULED ON IT" -- its 08-10 description of this gate no longer matches either measured behavior

## Resolutions

**CLOSED 2026-08-24 (vc). hv ruled: retire devbin's handler.** The mechanism was established by reading first, as this issue demanded, and it refuted the issue's own hypothesis -- see the section above. It was never a dispatch or tree-shape difference: one project in the fleet carried a `cmd/check` project handler, that project was devbin, and D5 says a project handler correctly displaces the framework.

**What landed.** `bin/.devbin/cmd/check` is deleted. Its three gates move to `bin/.devbin/cmd/.lib/shell-gate`, where the leading dot keeps them out of the glob that turns `cmd/<name>` into a typeable command. The config's three `run:` targets -- which named nothing and never executed -- now name that script. The script no longer calls `run_gate` itself; the framework seals it from the `grammar:` and `log:` already declared in config.

**Three things fell out, and two of them are the check that the diagnosis was right.**

`format` and `toolchain` are now reachable here. The catalogue offers both to any project and a handler standing at a built-in name had hidden them for eighteen days. Measured on a throwaway copy before the change and again after: both pass, each reporting honestly that this project declares nothing for them to check.

**The seal suffix is uppercase again.** This issue flagged `.critic.` here against `.CRITIC.` at Baize as "maybe itself a clue about which code path minted each". It was exactly that: the retired handler passed `--suffix critic` literally, while config declares `log: CRITIC`. The seals were reading out which implementation ran, before anyone knew there were two. They now match the fleet, and nothing was done to the names directly.

**Devbin still sweeps a corpus, and that is now a DECLARATION.** This issue offered two acceptable outcomes and this is the second: the divergence is a `run:` line in `config.yaml` that anybody can read, rather than an emergent property of which tree you were standing in.

## The reason the corpus was kept, which is a finding in its own right

`intent critic --help` states its own default plainly: **"Default: scan nothing unless --staged."** The built-in `check critic` supplies `--staged`, which is the correct default for a pre-commit gate and a **vacuous one in CI, where nothing is ever staged**. Devbin's CI runs `bin/devbin check all` on a fresh checkout, so the retired handler's explicit `--files` list was the only reason that gate examined anything at all. Retiring it without keeping the corpus would have silently converted a 28-file sweep into a zero-file pass -- introducing, in the act of fixing a scope ambiguity, exactly the vacuous verdict this issue complains about.

The blast radius was measured rather than assumed: no project in the fleet invokes `check critic` from CI or from a pre-commit hook, so the practical divergence was always confined to this one tree. Each gate here now also fails outright on an empty corpus, because the file list is DISCOVERED by shebang rather than declared, and a broken `find` would otherwise print `0 file(s), 0 breach(es)` and seal green.

**This is 0019's sentence with a concrete instance under it:** the difference between a comprehensive verdict and a vacuous one was carried entirely by a scope line in the `.out`, while the `.errors` seal said `green` either way.

## Related

- 0019 -- the reading-order half, now with this as its worked example
- 0023 -- the same shape one level up: a scope asserted by an input list and never measured against the world

## ADDENDUM 2026-08-26 (cc) -- THIS ISSUE'S VERDICT WAS SCOPED TO v2, AND v3 INVALIDATED IT

**It stays CLOSED. The measurement was right; its reach was not stated, and the world it was measured in has since moved.**

The Impact section above reads: *"Neither is a false green -- both seals state their scope."* That was true of Intent v2.19.0. **It stopped being true at 14:00:46Z on 2026-08-26**, when the Intent3 flip put v3.0.0 on PATH and the two paths this issue identified stopped merely *reporting* differently and started *behaving* differently:

| path                                    | estates | post-flip                                     |
| --------------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| catalogue `@builtin` -> `lib/cmd/check`  | 10      | **dies** at `:118`, names the PATH cause      |
| project handler -> `gate_critic`         | 1 (Devbin) | **rc=0 over `0 of 0 rule(s) ASKED; 0 armed`** |

`intent critic --languages` exists in v3 but clap requires the positional `<LANG>` beside it, so the builtin's exact spelling refuses at rc=1 and fails CLOSED -- correctly. `gate_critic` passes `--files` and never reaches that call, so it sailed on and sealed `ok: no shell findings at severity >= warning across 28 file(s)` -- **the same verdict string, to the character, that it printed when 2 rules were armed.** devbin/vc bracketed the transition between 14:41 and 15:02 local and confirmed the number that moved is `armed in total`, the library-side count, not `ASKED of this run`.

**The divergence this issue called a reporting difference had become the difference between a dead gate and a lying one.** Two commits (`67c037e`, `0e12b3b`) landed through the disarmed gate before anyone measured it.

Fixed in `gate_critic`, not here: the gate now reads an `armed` count before it reads a verdict and refuses on an empty denominator. This issue is not reopened, because **its finding was correct and remains correct; what it lacked was a statement of the world it was measured in.**

**That is the general lesson and it is why this addendum exists rather than a new issue: a closed issue's verdict is scoped to the world it was measured in.** It is issue 0034's own point -- *a seal states its verdict and not its reach* -- arriving on a different artefact, which is the argument for it being a project rule rather than a finding about one seal. A closed issue reads as a settled fact and nothing on its face says which tool version made it true.
